description: Conspiracy meme asserting 'FACEBOOK WAS CREATED BY DARPA TO TRACK A PERSON'S ENTIRE EXISTENCE'. Center: photo of Mark Zuckerberg at his April 2018 congressional testimony. Left: a Wired article 'Pentagon Kills LifeLog Project' dated 02.04.04, with highlighted text describing DARPA's LifeLog database ambitions. Right: Wikipedia's Facebook infobox with 'Founded February 4, 2004' highlighted — the meme's implied link being that Facebook launched the same day LifeLog was canceled. Bottom text: 'ARE YOU AWAKE YET? #GREATAWAKENING'.
text: FACEBOOK WAS CREATED BY DARPA TO TRACK "A PERSON'S ENTIRE EXISTENCE". WIRED. Pentagon Kills LifeLog Project. WIRED STAFF. BUSINESS. 02.04.04. 12:00 PM. PENTAGON KILLS LIFELOG PROJECT. THE PENTAGON CANCELED its so-called LifeLog project, an ambitious effort to build a database tracking a person's entire existence. Run by Darpa, the Defense Department's research arm, LifeLog aimed to gather in a single place just about everything an individual says, sees or does: the phone calls made, the TV shows watched, the magazines read, the plane tickets bought, the e-mail sent and received. Out of this seemingly endless ocean of information, computer scientists would plot distinctive routes in the data, mapping relationships, memories, events and experiences. LifeLog's backers said the all-encompassing diary could have turned into a near-perfect digital memory, giving its users computerized assistants with an almost flawless recall of what they had done in the past. But civil libertarians immediately pounced on the project when it debuted last. WWW.WIRED.COM/2004/02/PENTAGON-KILLS-LIFELOG-PROJECT/. facebook. Screenshot. [show]. Type of business. Public. Type of site. Social networking service. Available in. Multilingual (140). Traded as. NASDAQ: FB (Class A). NASDAQ-100 Component. S&P 100 Component. S&P 500 Component. Founded. February 4, 2004; 14 years ago. Headquarters. Menlo Park, California, United States of America. ARE YOU AWAKE YET? #GREATAWAKENING
flags: The claim that Facebook is a continuation of DARPA's LifeLog is an unproven conspiracy theory; the date coincidence is the meme's only offered evidence
